key_decisions: ONE FILE, ONE WRITER. Main is the sole file writer; the child skips its own file write when it is a fork (typeof process.send === "function"), and standalone `node server.js` in dev keeps writing.
VERBATIM RELAY - append the child line unchanged, preserving ITS timestamp. Re-logging through logger.info(category, message) stamps mains receive time and loses the childs.
app.log stays the active filename (getLogPath, routes/system.js x2, the in-app download and the docs all depend on it). Archives are app-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.log, immutable, pruned past 20.
BYTE CAP 256KB (~2000 lines), not a line cap - already tracked, O(1), no counter to carry across restarts. User asked for ~2000 lines; this is that.
Rotate-on-app-start was OFFERED AND DECLINED for now - quick restarts would churn tiny files and evict real history.
1.3.0 ALL THE WAY, NO BUMP - overwrite until right (user, 2026-07-31).
MPI-414 and MPI-418 are both release blockers - user decided, correct both times. Do not re-litigate.

resume_prompt: You are continuing Cubric Vision 1.3.0 on master. NOTHING IS PUBLISHED (latest live release is v1.2.0). Both named release blockers were implemented this session. MPI-414 (Retry routed on /engine/status, which is true from step 1 of the uv path, so an interrupted install got deps-only repair, a success toast and an engine that cannot boot) is FIXED and committed - it now routes on /engine/version-check and repair-deps refuses an unstamped engine; its live proof needs Linux or macOS, since the bug does not exist on Windows. MPI-418's SINK fix is FIXED AND PROVEN on a real Windows install - the [server] lines that never reached app.log now do, because main.js never set APP_USER_DATA on itself and its logger had resolved the path at module load. The Windows archive leg also came out green: 0.29.2 stamped and running, zero IMPORT FAILED, SDXL generation in 13.48s. BUT pointing both processes at one app.log exposed a DESTRUCTIVE race: _appendToFile does stat -> move -> append, so both processes rotate and the second moves the fresh file over the real backup. Measured end state was app.log 472 bytes / app.log.1 100 bytes with an entire session erased. The user also ruled that 256KB with one backup is too small to be useful. YOUR JOB: implement .agents/mpi-kanban/tasks/MPI-418/plan.md - main becomes the sole file writer, the child skips its file write when it is a fork, main relays child lines VERBATIM so their timestamps survive, app.log stays the active name, archives become app-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.log, prune past 20. Then rebuild all three artifacts and re-verify on Windows that the engine install is still readable on disk afterwards. Do not publish until it lands. Report outcomes in PLAIN LANGUAGE, not card IDs; do not use AskUserQuestion.
